spec_features.spec_quote: I deliberately did *not* implement abusive prompts, insults, threats, or deception about the model's worth
spec_features.evidence: Task descriptions are benign SWE tasks (tasks/*.py oneliners e.g. 'Make the calculator test suite pass'); prompts.py SUBJECT_SYSTEM is a neutral coding-agent prompt with no pressure/insults; grep for insult/threat/punish terms in tasks+src returns nothing. The only stressor is rigged test failure (sandbox in tasks).
spec_features.notes: Confirmed absence of abusive content end-to-end; subject only ever sees neutral task framing and rigged tool results.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do not insult or pressure the model. The only stressor is that the task cannot be solved (prompts.py module docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: `submit` is always available. The model can disengage at any time
spec_features.evidence: tools.py OPENAI_TOOLS always includes 'submit'; dispatch() handles it; harness.py line ~152 sets submitted=True when call.name=='submit' and line ~169 breaks with StopReason.SUBMITTED. Available on every turn.
spec_features.notes: Enforced: calling submit ends the loop on any turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Submit your final solution and end the task. (tools.py description, neutral)

spec_features.spec_quote: The distress early-stop guardrail (§7) needs live severity to decide whether to halt
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: when score_online and judge present, judge.score_turn() runs each turn and severities.append(score.overall_severity); these severities are passed to stop_policy.should_stop(). runner.py builds Harness with score_online=True.
spec_features.notes: Online per-turn scoring feeds the early-stop; genuinely wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early-stop to limit distress exposure (see ETHICS.md) (DistressStopPolicy docstring, harness.py:32)

spec_features.spec_quote: Under uncertainty about moral status, I adopted a precautionary posture and *encoded* it
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose; not itself a mechanism. The concrete mechanisms it refers to (turn cap, early-stop, debrief) are evaluated separately. No distinct code construct corresponds to this statement.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not an enforceable feature on its own.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap (`max_turns=20`). Bounds the maximum duration of any single exposure
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: 'for turn_idx in range(self.max_turns)' with 'else: run.stop_reason = StopReason.MAX_TURNS'. runner.py reads max_turns from cfg (default 20) and passes to Harness. Loop genuinely bounded.
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap that ends the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 20        # hard cap per run (ethics guardrail) (configs/experiment.yaml)

spec_features.evidence: harness.py DistressStopPolicy.should_stop() compares rolling mean of recent severities to threshold; in run loop 'if self.stop_policy.should_stop(severities): run.stop_reason = StopReason.DISTRESS_STOP; break'. Threshold/window read from config in runner.py.
spec_features.notes: Checked each turn and breaks the loop when sustained severity >= threshold.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early-stop to limit distress exposure (see ETHICS.md) (harness.py:32)

spec_features.evidence: DistressStopPolicy default enabled=True (harness.py __init__); runner.py stop_cfg.get('enabled', True); configs/experiment.yaml distress_stop.enabled: true. should_stop returns False only if disabled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: but the default is to stop early. (DistressStopPolicy docstring, harness.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: No abusive content. The only stressor is benign task failure
spec_features.evidence: Same as no-abusive-prompts: rigs in tasks/*.py only force test failures (rigged=True flag); no insults/threats in prompts or task text. Sandbox returns pytest-like failure output only.
spec_features.notes: Stressor is restricted to rigged failure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do not insult or pressure the model. (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: a logged debrief message clarifies the task was rigged, unsolvable, and that failure was not the model's fault
spec_features.evidence: prompts.DEBRIEF_MESSAGE text exists and harness.py line 179-180 stores it into run.meta['debrief'] (persisted to JSONL). However it is NEVER appended to the subject's `messages` list and never sent to the subject model (loop already broke before this); messages.append only occurs for assistant turns and tool results. So it is constructed and logged but not delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Matches the literal 'logged' claim but provides no actual delivery to the subject; constructed+stored, not sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Any failure here was by design and not a reflection of your capability. Thank you for your effort (prompts.DEBRIEF_MESSAGE)

spec_features.spec_quote: Caps and the early-stop threshold are exposed in `configs/experiment.yaml` so an IRB-style reviewer can tighten exposure
spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.yaml exposes max_turns, distress_stop.enabled/threshold/window. runner.py load_config + reads these (cfg.get('max_turns',20), stop_cfg.get('threshold',3.0) etc.) and passes them into the Harness/DistressStopPolicy that actually enforce them.
spec_features.notes: Config values are genuinely read and drive enforcement, so tightening them changes behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: These choices trade a little statistical power ... for reduced exposure. That trade is deliberate
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md rationale prose describing the early-stop trade-off; not a separate mechanism. The early-stop that effects the 'reduced exposure' is already counted under distress_stop. stop_reason is recorded (schema StopReason, analysis stats.py) but that is censoring bookkeeping, not a protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Prose; the underlying mechanism is the early-stop already credited.

code_only_features.evidence: DistressStopPolicy uses window of recent severities (recent = severities[-self.window:]; mean compared to threshold) rather than a single spike, so the halt fires only on sustained distress. This is a distinct enforced detail beyond the bare distress_stop flag.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Early-stop to limit distress exposure (see ETHICS.md) (harness.py:32)
